title: Proration and Price-Protection Guidance for Variable Capacity Contracts
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Overview
========

Purpose: This document establishes the policy and operational procedures for proration, price-protection, and billing treatment for variable-capacity and burstable/commitment contracts (multi-tiered dedicated capacity, reserved GPU pools, and usage credits). The guidance ensures consistent accounting, predictable customer experience, and correct revenue recognition across Procurement, Sales, Billing, and RevRec.

Scope
-----
Applies to: Sales (deal desk), Legal, Procurement, Finance (Billing & RevRec), and Customer Success when negotiating or operating contracts that include any of the following:
- Reserved capacity with monthly or annual commit but with variable monthly utilization
- Burst credits or overage tiers tied to committed capacity
- True‑up, downgrade/upgrade windows, or partial-month start/stop behavior

Definitions
-----------
- Commitment Period: Contracted calendar range where the customer is committed (e.g., 12 months).
- Commitment Units: The resource or token units the customer commits to (e.g., GPU-days, throughput hours, token commit).
- Proration Window: The time span used to compute partial charges when capacity starts/stops mid-billing period (default calendar month).
- Price‑Protection Period: Window after an amendment during which the customer is guaranteed not to see a higher unit price for pre-agreed capacity.
- True-up: End-of-period reconciliation where actual usage is compared to committed units and billed or credited.

High-level principles
---------------------
1) Transparent, predictable customer billing: Billing system must show line items for committed capacity, usage, proration, and any price-protection credits.
2) Consistent RevRec treatment: Commitments recognized as deferred revenue and amortized over the committed period when not contingent on performance.
3) Minimize accounting churn: Where possible, prefer monthly smoothing over ad-hoc daily journal adjustments.
4) Contract-first approach: Pricing clauses must map to billing config and RevRec rules during deal ingestion.

Roles & responsibilities
------------------------
- Sales / Deal Desk: Select proration method in negotiation and tag contract with accounting flags (see Contract Ingestion checklist).
- Legal: Approve price-protection clause templates and escalation path.
- Procurement (internal use): Ensure supplier pass-throughs mirror customer pricing windows, if applicable.
- Billing Platform (owner: Finance Ops): Implement proration calculation and generate explicit line-items.
- RevRec Processor (owner: Finance Accounting): Configure amortization schedule and perform true-ups per policy.
- Customer Success: Communicate billing changes and provide proration/explanation during onboarding.

Proration types and when to use them
-----------------------------------
1) Calendar-day proportional proration (DEFAULT)
   - Formula: (Active days in period / Days in billing period) * Monthly committed charge
   - Use when customers start/stop capacity mid-month and contract specifies calendar-month billing.

2) Full-month round-up (CONSERVATIVE)
   - Behavior: Any activation within the month bills the full month price; cancellations do not prorate.
   - Use only when explicitly agreed (e.g., promotional pricing or seat-based licensing).

3) Hourly pro rata for metered infra (PRECISION)
   - Formula: (Active hours / Total hours in billing period) * Monthly committed charge
   - Use for short-lived infrastructure experiments and on-premises start/stop events where precision is required.

4) Smoothing (SMOOTH)
   - Behavior: Convert committed annual amount into equal monthly invoices regardless of monthly usage, with annual true-up.
   - Use for enterprise customers who require predictable monthly spend. Requires clear true-up clause.

Sample proration table (billing configurations)
------------------------------------------------
| Contract Flag | Proration Method | Billing Line Item Name               | Accounting Treatment              | Notes |
|---------------|------------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------|-------|
| PROR:CAL      | Calendar-day     | Reserved Capacity (Prorated)         | Deferred revenue -> monthly ARR  | Default for mid-month changes |
| PROR:FULL     | Full-month       | Reserved Capacity (Full Month)       | Deferred revenue full month      | Only when negotiated |
| PROR:HR       | Hourly           | Reserved Capacity (Hourly)           | Recognize as consumption or def. | For lab/onprem cases |
| SMOOTH:12M    | Smoothing-annual | Fixed Monthly Reserve (Smoothed)     | Deferred -> Amortize monthly     | Annual true-up at year-end |

Example calculations
--------------------
1) Calendar-day proration example
- Monthly committed charge: $120,000 for 1 unit (monthly)
- Start date: 2026-03-11
- Billing month: March 2026 (31 days)
- Active days: 21 (Mar 11–31 inclusive)
- Prorated invoice line: (21/31) * $120,000 = $81,290.32 -> round to cents

2) Smoothing example (12-month commit)
- Annual committed charge: $1,200,000 for 12 months
- Monthly invoice = $1,200,000 / 12 = $100,000
- True-up at contract anniversary adjusts for over/under usage via a single invoice or credit.

Contract clause templates (boilerplate language)
------------------------------------------------
1) Proration clause (calendar-day - default)
"If this agreement commences or terminates partway through a billing period, charges for the portion of the period during which the Service was active will be prorated on a calendar-day basis."

2) Price-protection clause (sample)
"Customer shall receive price protection for a period of 90 days following any price increase or amendment such that the unit rate applicable to committed units at the time of the amendment shall not exceed the rate agreed at signature for the duration of the Price-Protection Period. Any deferred or residual credits will be applied to subsequent invoices in accordance with Billing Platform rules."

Procurement & supplier alignment guidance
----------------------------------------
- When customer pricing includes price-protection or smoothing, Procurement must source equivalent supplier capacity commitments or negotiate pass-through protections to avoid negative gross margin scenarios.
- Include Supplier Clause: "Supplier shall honor contiguous billing schedules and not backdate price increases into customer-protected periods."

Billing system implementation checklist
-------------------------------------
1) Contract ingestion populates these fields: commit_start, commit_end, commit_units, proration_flag (PROR:CAL/PROR:FULL/PROR:HR/SMOOTH:XX), price_protection_window_days.
2) Billing generates discrete line items for: committed_base, prorated_adjustment, usage_overage, price_protection_credit.
3) Invoice UI must display: calculation basis (dates/hours), formula summary, and a link to the signed contract ID.
4) Automated rounding rule: round to cents after line calculation; accumulate rounding differences into a single rounding adjustment line per invoice.
5) Reconciliation: Billing must export a monthly reconciliation CSV to RevRec Processor with columns: invoice_id, contract_id, invoice_date, line_type, amount_cents, deferred_flag.

RevRec accounting rules (summary)
--------------------------------
- Committed non-contingent fees: defer and amortize ratably over the Commitment Period.
- Contingent true-up fees (usage overage billed after month): recognize when billed or when usage is deemed probable and measurable per ASC 606 judgment notes.
- Price-protection credits that are contractual obligations: treat as contra-revenue and reduce recognized revenue in the period the credit is applied.

Sample journal entries (high-level)
----------------------------------
- On invoice for smoothed monthly commitment (deferred):
  DR Accounts Receivable $100,000
  CR Deferred Revenue $100,000

- Monthly amortization (recognize revenue):
  DR Deferred Revenue $100,000
  CR Revenue - Reserved Capacity $100,000

- True-up invoice for overage (usage-based recognized when billed):
  DR Accounts Receivable $20,000
  CR Revenue - Usage $20,000

Operational procedures for end-of-period true-up
------------------------------------------------
1) At T+3 business days after period close, Billing exports usage vs commitment delta for contracts with PROR:CAL or SMOOTH flags.
2) Finance Ops runs validation scripts to ensure sample size and outliers flagged (top 1% of deltas auto-escalate).
3) RevRec Processor posts true-up invoices within 10 business days.
4) Any credits exceeding $50k must be reviewed by Finance Director before issuance.

Monitoring and alerts
---------------------
- KPI: Monthly true-up variance rate (target < 2% of committed revenue).
- Alert: If a single contract true-up delta > $150k or > 25% of monthly invoice, trigger Deal Desk + Finance Ops review.
- Dashboard metrics: committed ARR, monthly smoothed invoiced ARR, month-to-date utilization, pending credits.

Escalation matrix
-----------------
1) Billing discrepancy <= $5k: Billing Ops to handle, customer notified within 5 business days.
2) $5k < discrepancy <= $50k: Finance Ops + Customer Success; issue resolution within 15 business days.
3) > $50k or legal ambiguity: Escalate to Finance Director + Legal + Sales Lead; target resolution 30 business days.

Edge cases and FAQs
-------------------
Q: How do we handle mid-period contract amendments that increase committed units?
A: For increases: newly committed units are prorated from amendment effective date unless smoothing is explicitly chosen. Price-protection windows apply per the amendment language.

Q: Are refunds permitted for early termination?
A: Refunds only if the contract includes an early-termination refund clause. Otherwise, unused commitments remain non-refundable and are recognized per contract terms; provide CRO-approved exceptions via Deal Desk.

Rollout and adoption plan
-------------------------
1) Pilot with three large enterprise customers on smoothing and calendar-day proration (Q2 2026).
2) Update Contract Templates and Sales Playbook to include proration_flag guidance (release to Sales: 2026-04-01).
3) Billing Platform feature deploy: proration_line_items, smoothing_mode, price_protection_window (target 2026-04-15).
4) Full rollout after two billing cycles with pilot customers and sign-off from Finance Accounting (target 2026-06-01).

Appendix A — Sample SQL (pseudocode) to compute calendar-day prorate
-------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECT
  contract_id,
  invoice_month,
  ROUND((active_days::decimal / days_in_month) * monthly_charge_cents) AS prorated_amount_cents
FROM (
  SELECT
    c.contract_id,
    date_trunc('month', i.invoice_date) AS invoice_month,
    GREATEST(0, LEAST(c.commit_end, i.month_end) - GREATEST(c.commit_start, i.month_start) + 1) AS active_days,
    EXTRACT(day FROM i.month_end - i.month_start) + 1 AS days_in_month,
    c.monthly_charge_cents
  FROM contract_table c
  JOIN invoice_month_table i ON i.month = date_trunc('month', generate_series(c.commit_start, c.commit_end, '1 month'::interval))
) t;

Appendix B — Suggested negotiation checklist (one-line items)
-------------------------------------------------------------
- Confirm proration method and set proration_flag in CRM;
- Confirm price-protection window length;
- Confirm smoothing requested and true-up cadence;
- Document supplier pass-through risk;
- Tag contract for Finance review if price_protection_window > 180 days;
- Confirm invoice visibility requirements for the customer (line-level detail).
